content: A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea. Examples include boy, girl, school, tree, and happiness.
A verb is a word that shows action or a state of being. Examples include run, jump, think, sleep, is, and are.
An adjective is a word that describes a noun. Examples include big, small, red, fast, and happy.
India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru were key leaders in the freedom struggle.
The Taj Mahal, located in Agra, India, was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. As sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, gases and particles scatter the blue light in all directions because it travels as shorter, smaller waves.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) and freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (32 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure.
Cricket is a popular bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven players. India won the Cricket World Cup in 1983 and 2011.
The Olympics are a major international sporting event held every four years. Neeraj Chopra won a historic gold medal for India in javelin throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
The Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life. It has one natural satellite, the Moon.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level, located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and China (Tibet).
